BiblicalUsage: mashshûwʼâh is ruin, desolation. In Psalms 73:18 God sets the wicked in slippery places and casts them down into destruction, and in Psalms 74:3 the psalmist asks Him to lift His feet to the perpetual desolations the enemy has done wickedly in the sanctuary. The word is the ruin left after pride.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mashshûwʼâh shows me that the proud stand on slippery ground, and that ruin is the end of the path they chose.
